label: M Code
headline: Power Query M Cheat Sheet
description: Quick reference for Power Query M — the functional language behind Power BI and Excel data transformations. Covers values, operators, text, numbers, dates, lists, records, and tables.

items.name: Power Query
items.definition: Power Query is a tool for extract-transform-load (ETL). It lets you import and prepare data for use in Power BI, Excel, Azure Data Lake Storage, and Dataverse.

items.name: Power Query M
items.definition: M (short for 'Mashup') is the functional programming language used in Power Query. Case-sensitive. Used for data transformation, not data analysis (that's DAX).

items.name: Expression
items.definition: A single formula that returns a value. All M code is composed of expressions.

items.name: Query (let...in)
items.syntax:
let
  Source = Csv.Document(File.Contents("data.csv")),
  Result = Table.PromoteHeaders(Source)
in
  Result
items.definition: A query is a sequence of expressions defined with let...in. Each step can reference previous steps. The in expression is what the query returns.

items.name: Comments
items.definition: // for single-line comments. /* */ for multi-line comments. Use them to document steps in the Advanced Editor.

items.name: Number
items.definition: Integer or decimal number literals. M has no distinction between int and float at the language level.

items.name: Text
items.definition: Text values are double-quoted. Embed a double-quote by doubling it: "".

items.name: Logical
items.definition: Boolean literals. Lowercase only — True and False are not valid in M.

items.name: Null
items.definition: Represents a missing or unknown value. Many functions return null instead of throwing an error on empty input.

items.name: Date
items.definition: Date literal using #date(year, month, day). Can also use #datetime, #datetimezone, #duration, #time.

items.name: Datetime
items.definition: Datetime literal: #datetime(year, month, day, hour, minute, second).

items.name: Duration
items.definition: Represents an elapsed time span. Use with Date.AddDays or subtraction between two datetime values.

items.name: List
items.definition: A list is an ordered sequence of values in curly braces. Can contain mixed types. {1..10} creates a range.

items.name: Record
items.definition: A record is a set of named fields in square brackets. Like a single row with column names.

items.name: Table
items.definition: Creates a table from a list of column names and a list of row lists.

items.name: let...in
items.definition: let assigns named intermediate values. Each name can reference earlier names. in specifies the final returned value.

items.name: Naming conventions
items.definition: Variable names are UpperCamelCase by convention. Wrap names with spaces or special characters in #"...".

items.name: Step reference
items.syntax:
let
  Source = Excel.CurrentWorkbook(){[Name="Table1"]}[Content],
  Typed = Table.TransformColumnTypes(Source, {{"Date", type date}})
in
  Typed
items.definition: Each step name becomes a reference. Steps are the building blocks of every Power Query transformation.

items.name: Arithmetic
items.definition: Standard math operators. Use Number.Mod for modulo and Number.IntegerDivide for integer division.

items.name: Comparison
items.syntax:
3 = 3    // true (equal)
3 <> 4   // true (not equal)
3 > 1    // true
3 >= 3   // true
3 < 4    // true
3 <= 4   // true
items.definition: Returns a logical value (true/false). M comparison is case-sensitive for text.

items.name: Logical
items.syntax:
not (2 = 2)              // false
(1 < 1) and (1 >= 1)     // false
(1 >= 1) or (1 < 1)      // true
items.definition: and, or, not operators for combining logical conditions.

items.name: Text concatenation &
items.definition: The & operator joins text values. Equivalent to Text.Combine for two strings.

items.name: List concatenation &
items.definition: The & operator also concatenates two lists end-to-end.

items.name: is / as (type)
items.syntax:
1 is number      // true
"hello" is text  // true
Value.Is(x, type number)
items.definition: is checks if a value matches a type. as casts a value to a type (errors if it doesn't match).

items.name: ? (optional)
items.syntax:
Record.Field(rec, "Name")?
// Returns null instead of error if field missing
items.definition: The ? operator after an expression converts errors into null rather than stopping the query.

items.name: Text.Length
items.definition: Returns the number of characters in a text string.

items.name: Text.Upper / Lower / Proper
items.definition: Converts text to uppercase, lowercase, or title case (first letter of each word capitalised).

items.name: Text.Start / End
items.definition: Extracts characters from the start or end of a string.

items.name: Text.Middle
items.definition: Extracts a substring starting at a zero-based position for the given length.

items.name: Text.Range
items.definition: Extracts a substring by zero-based start index and length. Similar to Text.Middle.

items.name: Text.Split
items.definition: Splits a text value on a delimiter and returns a list of text values.

items.name: Text.Combine
items.definition: Joins a list of text values with a separator string.

items.name: Text.Replace
items.syntax:
Text.Replace("Have a nice trip", "trip", "day")
// "Have a nice day"
items.definition: Replaces all occurrences of a substring with a new substring.

items.name: Text.Contains
items.definition: Returns true if the text string contains the specified substring.

items.name: Text.StartsWith / EndsWith
items.definition: Checks whether a text value starts or ends with a given substring.

items.name: Text.Trim / TrimStart / TrimEnd
items.definition: Removes whitespace (or specified characters) from both ends, the start, or the end of a string.

items.name: Text.PadStart / PadEnd
items.definition: Pads a string to a minimum length using a fill character on the left or right.

items.name: Text.From
items.definition: Converts any value to its text representation.

items.name: Text.ToList
items.definition: Splits a text string into a list of individual characters.

items.name: Number.Abs
items.definition: Returns the absolute (positive) value of a number.

items.name: Number.Round
items.definition: Rounds to the specified number of decimal places using standard half-up rounding.

items.name: Number.RoundUp / Down
items.definition: Always rounds away from or toward zero, regardless of the digit value.

items.name: Number.IntegerDivide
items.definition: Returns the integer quotient — discards the remainder.

items.name: Number.Mod
items.definition: Returns the remainder after integer division.

items.name: Number.Power
items.definition: Raises a number to the given power.

items.name: Number.Sqrt
items.definition: Returns the positive square root of a number.

items.name: Number.Ln / Exp
items.definition: Natural logarithm and exponential (e^n).

items.name: Number.Log
items.definition: Returns the logarithm of a number to the specified base.

items.name: Number.IsNaN
items.definition: Returns true if the value is NaN (Not a Number). Useful after division that may produce undefined results.

items.name: Number.From
items.definition: Converts text, logical, or date values to a number.

items.name: Number.ToText
items.definition: Formats a number as text. Format codes: G (general), F (fixed), N (number), P (percent), E (exponential).

items.name: Value.Equals
items.definition: Compares two values for equality with optional precision control — useful for floating-point comparisons.

items.name: Date.From
items.definition: Converts text or datetime values to a date.

items.name: DateTime.LocalNow
items.definition: Returns the current local date and time. Refreshes on every query evaluation.

items.name: Date.Year / Month / Day
items.definition: Extracts the year, month (1–12), or day of month from a date value.

items.name: Date.DayOfWeek
items.definition: Returns the day of the week as a number. Second argument sets the first day: Day.Monday, Day.Sunday.

items.name: Date.WeekOfYear
items.definition: Returns the week number within the year for the given date.

items.name: Date.QuarterOfYear
items.definition: Returns the quarter number (1–4) for a date.

items.name: Date.AddDays / Months / Years
items.definition: Adds the specified number of days, months, or years to a date.

items.name: Date.StartOfMonth / EndOfMonth
items.definition: Returns the first or last date of the month containing the given date.

items.name: Date.StartOfYear / EndOfYear
items.definition: Returns the first or last date of the year containing the given date.

items.name: Duration.Days / TotalHours
items.definition: Extracts a component from a duration. TotalHours/TotalMinutes/TotalSeconds return the full span, not just the component.

items.name: Date difference
items.definition: Subtracting two dates returns a duration. Wrap in Duration.Days / TotalHours etc. to get a numeric count.

items.name: List creation
items.definition: Lists are created with curly braces. Use .. for ranges. Mixed types are allowed.

items.name: List.Count
items.definition: Returns the number of items in a list.

items.name: List.First / Last
items.definition: Returns the first or last element. Optional second argument is a default value if the list is empty.

items.name: List.FirstN / LastN
items.definition: Returns the first or last N items from a list.

items.name: List.Distinct
items.definition: Returns a list with duplicate values removed, preserving the first occurrence.

items.name: List.Select
items.definition: Returns a new list containing only items that satisfy the condition. Uses each with _ as the current item.

items.name: List.Transform
items.definition: Applies a function to every item and returns the resulting list.

items.name: List.Sort
items.definition: Returns a sorted copy of the list. Default is ascending order.

items.name: List.Reverse
items.definition: Returns a new list with the items in reverse order.

items.name: List.Contains / ContainsAny / All
items.syntax:
List.Contains({1,2,3}, 2)            // true
List.ContainsAny({1,2,3}, {3,4})     // true
List.ContainsAll({1,2,3}, {1,2})     // true
items.definition: Checks whether a list contains a single value, any from a second list, or all from a second list.

items.name: List.MatchesAny / All
items.syntax:
List.MatchesAny({1,2,13}, each _ > 10)  // true
List.MatchesAll({1,2,13}, each _ > 0)   // false
items.definition: Returns true if any or all items satisfy the condition.

items.name: List.RemoveNulls
items.definition: Returns a new list with all null values removed.

items.name: List.RemoveRange
items.syntax:
List.RemoveRange({1,2,3,4,5}, 1, 2)
// {1,4,5} — remove 2 items starting at index 1
items.definition: Removes a range of items by zero-based start index and count.

items.name: List.Repeat
items.definition: Repeats the list the specified number of times.

items.name: List.Combine
items.definition: Flattens one level of nesting — takes a list of lists and returns a single flat list.

items.name: List.Split
items.definition: Splits a list into sub-lists of the given size.

items.name: List.Min / Max / Sum / Average
items.definition: Aggregate functions over a list. All ignore null values.

items.name: List.Product / StandardDeviation
items.definition: Multiplies all items together, or returns the standard deviation of a numeric list.

items.name: List.Union / Intersect / Difference
items.definition: Set operations on lists. Union merges unique values; Intersect keeps common values; Difference keeps items only in the first list.

items.name: List.Numbers
items.definition: Generates a list starting at start, with count items, incrementing by step.

items.name: List.Dates
items.definition: Generates a list of dates starting at a date, for a count of items, with a duration step.

items.name: List.Generate
items.definition: Generates a list by repeatedly applying a function until a condition is false. Arguments: initial, condition, next.

items.name: List.SingleOrDefault
items.definition: Returns the single item, or the default value if the list has zero or more than one item.

items.name: Record creation
items.definition: Records are created with square brackets using Name = Value pairs. Used to represent a single row of data.

items.name: Record.Field
items.definition: Retrieves a field value by name. Equivalent to record[FieldName] shorthand.

items.name: record[FieldName]
items.definition: Dot-style field access. Raises an error if the field doesn't exist — use Record.Field with ? for safe access.

items.name: Record.FieldNames / Values
items.definition: Returns a list of the record's field names or field values.

items.name: Record.HasFields
items.definition: Returns true if the record contains a field or all fields in a list.

items.name: Record.AddField
items.definition: Returns a new record with an additional field. Original record is not mutated.

items.name: Record.RemoveFields
items.definition: Returns a new record with the specified field(s) removed.

items.name: Record.RenameFields
items.definition: Returns a new record with specified fields renamed. Argument is a list of {old, new} name pairs.

items.name: Record.ToTable
items.definition: Converts a record to a two-column table with Name and Value columns.

items.name: Record.FromList
items.definition: Creates a record from a list of values and a matching list of field names.

items.name: Table.FromRecords
items.definition: Creates a table from a list of records. Each record becomes a row; field names become column headers.

items.name: Table.RowCount / ColumnCount
items.syntax:
Table.RowCount(myTable)    // number of rows
Table.ColumnCount(myTable) // number of columns
items.definition: Returns the number of rows or columns in a table.

items.name: Table.ColumnNames
items.definition: Returns a list of the table's column names in order.

items.name: Table.SelectRows
items.definition: Filters a table to rows where the condition is true. Uses each with field access via [ColumnName].

items.name: Table.AddColumn
items.definition: Adds a new column computed from each row. Fourth argument is the optional type annotation.

items.name: Table.TransformColumns
items.definition: Applies a transformation function to one or more columns by name.

items.name: Table.TransformColumnTypes
items.definition: Changes the data type of one or more columns. The most common step after Source in any query.

items.name: Table.RemoveColumns
items.definition: Returns the table without the specified columns.

items.name: Table.SelectColumns
items.definition: Returns only the specified columns, in the order listed.

items.name: Table.RenameColumns
items.definition: Renames one or more columns. Argument is a list of {old, new} name pairs.

items.name: Table.ReorderColumns
items.definition: Returns the table with columns in the specified order. Unlisted columns are dropped.

items.name: Table.Sort
items.definition: Sorts a table by one or more columns. Order.Ascending (default) or Order.Descending.

items.name: Table.Group
items.definition: Groups rows by one or more key columns and aggregates each group. Similar to GROUP BY in SQL.

items.name: Table.PromoteHeaders
items.definition: Promotes the first row of data to become the column headers.

items.name: Table.DemoteHeaders
items.definition: Converts the current column headers into the first data row, then assigns generic column names.

items.name: Table.FillDown / FillUp
items.definition: Fills null values downward or upward from the nearest non-null value in the specified columns.

items.name: Table.Pivot
items.definition: Rotates unique values of one column into new column headers, aggregating the value column. Same as Pivot Column in the UI.

items.name: Table.Unpivot / UnpivotOtherColumns
items.definition: Converts column headers into rows. UnpivotOtherColumns keeps the specified columns fixed and unpivots everything else.

items.name: Table.ExpandListColumn
items.definition: Expands a column containing lists — each list item becomes a separate row.

items.name: Table.ExpandRecordColumn
items.definition: Expands a column containing records — each specified field becomes its own column.

items.name: Table.NestedJoin
items.definition: Joins two tables on a key column. Returns the right-side matches as a nested table in a new column. JoinKind: Inner, LeftOuter, RightOuter, FullOuter, LeftAnti, RightAnti.

items.name: Table.Join
items.definition: Flat join that returns combined columns directly, without a nested table step.

items.name: Table.Distinct
items.definition: Removes duplicate rows. Optional second argument specifies which columns to consider for uniqueness.

items.name: Table.Buffer
items.definition: Forces the table to be fully evaluated and cached in memory. Prevents repeated evaluation of expensive upstream steps.

items.name: Function definition
items.syntax:
let
  Hypotenuse = (x, y) =>
    Number.Sqrt(Number.Power(x,2) + Number.Power(y,2))
in
  Hypotenuse(3, 4) // 5
items.definition: Functions are defined with (params) => expression. They can be assigned to names with let and called by name.

items.name: each shorthand
items.definition: each is syntactic sugar for a one-argument function where the argument is named _. Used heavily in List, Table, and Record functions.

items.name: each with record fields
items.definition: Inside Table functions, each automatically receives the current row as a record. Access columns with [ColumnName].

items.name: Type annotation
items.syntax:
(x as number, y as number) as number =>
  x + y
items.definition: Add type constraints to function parameters and return values with as. M checks types at runtime, not compile time.

items.name: Optional parameters
items.syntax:
(text as text, optional delimiter as nullable text) =>
  Text.Split(text, delimiter ?? ",")
items.definition: Mark parameters optional with the optional keyword. Use ?? to provide a default if null is passed.

items.name: ?? (null coalescing)
items.definition: Returns the left value if it is not null, otherwise returns the right value. Cleaner than if x = null then default else x.
